title: A night with Nat King Cole and brother Eddie Cole
summary: Budd sits in at a Hollywood party with Cole's trio and recalls Nat and Eddie Cole struggling in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: That's Earl's great solo, you know. So we wrote -- I wrote all of this stuff, and we were able to make enough money to get out of California. In the meantime we were invited out by Nat King Cole to go hang out with him at a party, he was playing a party for some big people there in Hollywood, and then we went out and was drinking and eating and having a night with Nat King Cole. And this is when he was playing the piano, and he had just first really started to try to sing, you know. Evidently he had done it before but not maybe in public, you know, and so he was playing and singing and everything, and everything went beautifully and these people was talking about Nat King Cole, they were behind him 100 percent, and he did have a beautiful trio.
Prince French was the bass player?

That's right. And I took my horn out and you know, for the cats we blew with them, what not, hung out. Because I knew Nat King Cole from Chicago. You remember when his brother and he organized a band, Eddie Cole left (Unintelligible) and came back to Chicago.

And they tried to organize a big band and just like you were saying King Cole was so raggedy that like be like (unintelligible). When he walked he would hum. He really was, like Milt said, he was really -- was scuffling.
They were really scuffling, and they did pretty nice, they did a pretty good little band there for a while. But I still say King Cole's singing style sort of came from Eddie. I think.
His brother was always the one we always figured was the most likely to succeed.
He played bass, he played piano, he sang and everything.
